summary: The release lifecycle and validation ordering are generally fail-closed, but duplicate package names are collapsed during repository-contract validation and can hide conflicting runtime metadata.

findings.title: Reject duplicate runtime package entries
findings.problem: The observed_packages dictionary retains only the last package for each normalized name. An earlier duplicate with a conflicting version or repository supplier is ignored when a later entry is valid, so ambiguous runtime-package data can pass the release contract.
findings.current_code: observed_packages = {normalized_name(package["name"]): package for package in packages ...}
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve every entry per normalized name, require exactly one entry for each expected runtime package at the pinned version, and check supplier attribution across all package entries. Add both package-order regressions.

positive_changes: Tag ancestry and draft resolution are checked before generation.
Both SBOM gates precede artifact upload in the read-only generation job.
The publication path downloads and verifies the uploaded asset before publishing.
testing_recommendations: Add duplicate runtime-name mutations for conflicting versions and supplier attribution in both package orders.
Use the first complete release lifecycle as an end-to-end operational acceptance test.
recommended_actions: Reject ambiguous duplicate entries for required runtime package names before publication.
